text: My roommate and I split groceries but she keeps buying expensive stuff like $9 oat milk and imported cheese and then wants to divide the receipt evenly. I don't want to start a fight because we still have eight months left on the lease and otherwise she's great. How do I bring this up without sounding cheap, and what's a fair system we could switch to?

I'm putting together a trivia night for my kid's school fundraiser, around 60 parents, mostly in their 30s and 40s. I need six rounds of eight questions each, and I want one round to be about our town (Millbrook, Ohio) which I'll write myself. Can you draft the other five rounds with a mix of easy and hard questions, and put the answers at the end so I can print them separately?

My uncle keeps insisting at family dinners that lightning never strikes the same place twice and that you're safe standing where it just hit. I'm pretty sure that's wrong but I want to come to the next dinner with actual facts, not just vibes. What does the evidence say, and is there anything true in what he's saying, or is it completely made up?

Please rewrite the paragraph below so it sounds friendlier for our customer newsletter, keep it under 90 words, don't use exclamation marks, and keep the part about the Tuesday closure exactly as written. Paragraph: Due to scheduled maintenance, the downtown branch will be closed on Tuesday, March 4. Services will resume Wednesday. We apologize for any inconvenience this may cause our members and their families.

I just found out I didn't get the promotion I've been working toward for two years, and the person who got it started six months ago. My manager said it was 'a close call' but didn't really explain. I have a one-on-one with her on Friday and I'm worried I'll either cry or say something I regret. What should I actually say in that meeting?

Can you write a short bedtime story, like 300 words, for my four year old about a snail named Pico who is scared of the rain even though snails usually love rain? She's been nervous about thunderstorms lately so I'd like it to be gently reassuring without being preachy. Please avoid anything with monsters or getting lost, and give it a cozy ending.

I read that we only use 10 percent of our brains and I've also read that's a myth. Then my psych professor said something about how at any given moment most neurons aren't firing, which sounds kind of like the 10 percent thing again. Can you untangle this for me? What's actually true, and where did the myth come from in the first place?

I have a spreadsheet with about 4,000 rows of customer orders. Column A is the order date stored as text like '03/15/2025', column B is the customer email, and column C is the order total. I want a formula that tells me, for each customer, how many orders they placed in 2025 and their total spend that year. I'm using Google Sheets, not Excel.

My grandmother turns 90 next month and the family asked me to give a toast at the party. She was a nurse for forty years, raised five kids mostly on her own after my grandpa died, and she still does the crossword in pen every morning. I'm not a confident public speaker. Could you help me write something about two minutes long that's warm and a little funny?

Is it actually worse for the environment to use a dishwasher or to wash dishes by hand? My partner and I argue about this constantly. We have an older dishwasher, maybe 12 years old, and we usually run it about four times a week. I'd like an honest answer even if it's 'it depends', but please tell me exactly what it depends on.

I'm going to paste my cover letter below. Only fix grammar and spelling mistakes, do not change the wording or tone otherwise, and list each change you made underneath. Here it is: Dear Hiring Manager, I am writting to apply for the Junior Analyst position at Brightwell Partners. Over the last two year I have developed strong skills in data cleaning and reporting, and I beleive I would be a good fit for you're team.

Our book club is reading a novel a month and people are getting bored of the same literary fiction. We're eight women in our 50s and 60s, we meet at someone's house, and we like discussion more than plot twists. Can you suggest ten books from different genres or countries that would spark good conversations, with one sentence on why each would work for a group like ours?

I've been learning Spanish for about a year on apps and I'm finally going to Mexico City for two weeks in June. I'm nervous that I'll freeze up when people talk fast, especially at restaurants and in taxis. What are some practical things I can do in the next six weeks to prepare, and what should I do in the moment if I don't understand someone?

My doctor said my vitamin D is a little low (24 ng/mL) and told me to take a supplement, but my coworker says supplements are a scam and I should just get more sun. I live in Seattle so sun is kind of limited most of the year. Who's right here? I'm not asking you to replace my doctor, I just want to understand the reasoning on both sides.

I run a small bakery and I want to start a loyalty program but I don't want to pay for an app. Most of my customers are regulars who come in two or three times a week, usually before work. Can you come up with three simple loyalty program ideas I could run with paper cards or a basic spreadsheet, and what the pros and cons of each would be?

My teenage son told me he wants to drop out of the school orchestra after six years of violin. He says he's just not into it anymore and wants more time for his friends and the robotics club. Part of me thinks he'll regret quitting, but I also don't want to force him to keep going. How do I have this conversation with him without making it a battle?

Why do some people say you should never wake a sleepwalker? My younger brother has started sleepwalking a couple of times a month and last night I found him trying to open the front door at 2am. My mom says waking him could give him a heart attack. That sounds extreme to me. What should we actually do when it happens again?

Summarize the following meeting notes in exactly three bullet points for my boss, who only cares about decisions and deadlines, not discussion. Notes: We talked about the website redesign for a while. Priya thinks the blue is too dark. We decided to launch the new homepage on May 12. Marcus will finish the pricing page by May 5. We still haven't decided about the blog. Budget stays at $18,000.

I want to plant a vegetable garden in my backyard in central Texas. I have a spot that gets about six hours of sun, the soil is pretty clay-heavy, and I've never gardened before. It's early February now. What should I plant first, what do I need to do to the soil, and what's a realistic plan for the first season so I don't get overwhelmed?

My best friend is getting married and asked me to be her maid of honor, but I just lost my job and honestly can't afford the bachelorette trip to Nashville that the other bridesmaids are planning. I don't want to let her down or make it about me. How do I tell her, and is there a way to still be a good maid of honor on a tight budget?

I keep seeing claims online that cracking your knuckles causes arthritis, and also that it definitely doesn't. I crack mine probably 30 times a day, it's a habit from stress. What do the actual studies say? I'd also like to know what the popping sound actually is, because nobody has ever explained that to me properly and I'm curious.

Can you help me plan a one week road trip starting and ending in Denver in late September? We're two adults and a dog, we like hiking but nothing too technical, and we'd rather drive at most four hours a day. We don't mind camping a couple of nights but want a real bed for at least four of them. Give me a day by day plan.

Translate this message to my landlord into polite formal French. Keep the dates and the dollar amount exactly the same, and don't add anything I didn't say. Message: Hello, I wanted to let you know the kitchen faucet has been leaking since March 3. I paid a plumber $140 to look at it but he said the pipe behind the wall needs to be replaced. Could you arrange a repair this month?

I'm a first time manager at a small software company and one of the people on my team, who used to be my peer, keeps missing standups and turning things in late. We used to go to lunch together all the time and I don't want to lose that friendship. How do I address the performance issue directly without it getting weird between us?

My friend says that the Great Wall of China is visible from space with the naked eye, and he says astronauts have confirmed it. I think I heard that was false but I'm not sure anymore. Can you give me a clear answer, including what astronauts have actually said about it, and explain why the idea became so popular in the first place?

I teach seventh grade science and I need a hands-on activity about density that costs less than $20 for a class of 28 students and fits in a 45 minute period. Our classroom doesn't have sinks, so nothing too messy. Could you describe one or two activities step by step, including the materials list and a couple of questions to ask students afterward?

My elderly neighbor, Mr. Okafor, has lived alone since his wife passed last year. Lately he's been coming over almost every evening to chat for an hour or more. I like him and I don't want him to feel lonely, but I work from home and it's getting hard to finish my work. How can I set a gentle boundary without hurting his feelings?

Is it true that you should wait 30 minutes after eating before you go swimming? My parents enforced this rule our whole childhood and now my wife and I are arguing about whether to do the same with our kids at the lake this summer. I'd love to know if there's any real science behind it or if it's just an old wives' tale.

Make a packing checklist for a three day business trip to Chicago in January. Format it as a simple list with checkboxes, split into clothing, toiletries, and work items, and keep it to at most 25 items total. I'll be presenting at a client meeting on the second day, so include whatever I'd need for that, but I'm only bringing a carry-on bag.

I'm trying to name my new pottery business. I make mostly functional stuff like mugs and bowls with speckled glazes, I'm based in a small coastal town in Maine, and I want the name to feel handmade and calm, not cutesy. Can you give me 15 name ideas, and for the three you like best, explain why and suggest a matching tagline?
